overview: Two types of responses to a stimulus, differing in whether conscious brain involvement is needed before the response occurs.
genZNote: Reflex action: your body reacts before your brain even finishes registering it. Voluntary action: you consciously decide, then act.

aspects.label: Conscious Brain Involvement
aspects.valueA: Involuntary and rapid — typically processed at the spinal cord level, without waiting for conscious brain input.
aspects.valueB: Requires conscious thought and decision-making, processed in the cerebrum.

aspects.label: Speed of Response
aspects.valueA: Very fast, since the pathway (reflex arc) bypasses higher brain processing.
aspects.valueB: Slower, since it requires full cognitive processing before a response.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Pulling your hand away from a hot object before you consciously feel the pain.
aspects.valueB: Deciding to pick up a cup of tea and drink it.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: A reflex action occurs so quickly precisely because the signal is processed at the spinal cord, not routed all the way up to the brain first — a key mechanism-based exam point.
overlay.memoryTrick: Reflex = fast, automatic, spinal cord shortcut. Voluntary = slow, deliberate, full brain involvement.
overlay.commonMisconception: You do still consciously perceive the sensation (like pain) during a reflex — you simply become aware of it after the reflex movement has already happened, not before.
